sections.label: Consistency
paragraphs: Patients forget their exercises or are unsure if they're doing them correctly.

sections.label: Transparency
paragraphs: Progress tracking is unclear or missing, lowering motivation.

sections.label: Speed
paragraphs: Physios want more efficient ways to assign, update, and monitor training plans.

sections.label: Reminders
paragraphs: Both groups requested better reminders and feedback loops.
Let physiotherapists assign, monitor, and adjust plans for many patients at once, including in bulk.
Help patients consistently complete their home rehab exercises. Motivate them and become part of their routine.
Provide both patients and physios with clear, engaging feedback and reminders that support ongoing progress and communication.

sections.label: Onboarding
paragraphs: Get people into the program smoothly, and let them finish daily tasks without help, across ages and levels of comfort with tech.

sections.label: Guidance
paragraphs: Make exercise flows painless, including for people with limited accessibility needs. Keep the tone and visual language positive, encouraging, and personal.

sections.label: Insights & Data
paragraphs: Give physios actionable data and clear navigation across task flows, so they can make fast, informed decisions.

sections.label: Reassurance
paragraphs: Deliver feedback, reminders, and support in the channels each person prefers, including a direct physio chat.

sections.label: Separate experiences, shared goals
paragraphs: We first defined the relationship logic between patients and physiotherapists. To reduce cognitive load, we kept patient user flows simple, while focusing on control and efficiency for specialists.

sections.label: Physiotherapist portal
paragraphs: This portal allows specialists to manage patients, track compliance, create or edit programs, monitor progress, and communicate via chat.

sections.label: Patient-facing app
paragraphs: The home screen provides a complete overview of the recovery journey. Early testing revealed that patients prefer seeing their data in one place, as long as it remains encouraging and not overwhelming.

sections.label: Design system
paragraphs: I set a shared UI language and consistent patterns across the platform: reusable modules, hierarchies, and interactions. That supports usability, accessibility, and trust. It also let us prototype quickly and work together through the roadmap.

sections.label: Functional Prototype
paragraphs: I made a semi-polished prototype and tested a staging version of selected flows. That let us apply the important feedback before launch.

sections.label: Who I tested with
paragraphs: I ran usability tests with three patients and three physiotherapists on the core flows. Onboarding, daily exercises, program creation, and checking progress.

sections.label: What worked
paragraphs: Patients got through onboarding in about a minute and moved through exercise flows without getting stuck. The instructions were clear enough. Physiotherapists picked up the program builder quickly and liked dragging exercises around to build a routine.

sections.label: Impressions and ease
paragraphs: Feedback was positive in both groups. People liked the clear instructions and the navigation. Some asked for more visual cues and reminders on the dashboard. Those went into the next iteration, to raise compliance and satisfaction.

sections.label: On a good track
paragraphs: The biggest win is that patients started feeling like they had a coach in their pocket. Physiotherapists felt like they had visibility into what was happening at home. That's what drove compliance up more than any feature or detail.
